_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); integrated oil and gas signals

pit_profile.why: ExxonMobil: 'Our principal business involves exploration for, and production of, crude oil and natural gas; manufacture, trade, transport and sale of crude oil, natural gas, petroleum products, petrochemicals and a wide variety of specialty products; and pursuit of lower-emission business opportunities including carbon capture and storage, hydrogen and biofuels'; 'The oil, gas, and petrochemical businesses are fundamentally commodity businesses. This means ExxonMobil’s operations and earnings may be significantly affected by changes in oil, gas, and petrochemical prices and by changes in margins on refined products'; 'The energy and petrochemical industries are highly competitive'; among its risk factors, 'increased competitiveness of, or government policy support for, alternative energy sources' and 'Driven by concern over the risks of climate change, a number of countries have adopted, or are considering the adoption of, regulatory frameworks to reduce greenhouse gas emissions including emissions from the production and use of oil and gas and their products', which 'could negatively affect our investment returns, make our hydrocarbon-based products more expensive or less competitive, lengthen project implementation times, and reduce demand for hydrocarbons, as well as shift hydrocarbon demand toward relatively lower-carbon alternatives' (its own FY2021 10-K): earnings that move with the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; re-filed under the energy transition: the theme registry dates its market pricing to ExxonMobil's removal from the Dow Jones Industrial Average (S&P Dow Jones Indices, announced 2020-08-24: 'Salesforce.com (NYSE:CRM) will replace Exxon Mobil Corp. (NYSE:XOM)', effective 2020-08-31; the announcement gives as its reason 'prompted by DJIA constituent Apple Inc.'s (NASD:AAPL) decision to split its stock 4:1'), while ExxonMobil's own FY2021 10-K says 'reduce demand for hydrocarbons'

TRANSITION-exposed franchise (obsolescence risk 3/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.30x; -34% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +2.04; conservative 2yr +157%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -53.9%/yr (worst year FY12-FY22 ex-FY20, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +13.3%/yr (Q4 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr ex-FY20 median

BULL.desc: EPS +13.3%/yr (FY12-FY22 ex-FY20 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +61.1%/yr (best 2-yr run FY12-FY22 ex-FY20); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: XOM (retrospective, 2023-02-17) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.30x (79.3% downside to Bear $23 / +266.6% upside to Bull $408) | Adj composite 3.40 vs market 1.36: gap +2.04 [UNDERVALUED] | -34% above the EPP floor $169 (12x FY23E $14.06) | Conservative 2-yr case: +157.0% total (+78.5%/yr) | At 7.9x FY23E the 15% hurdle price $147 sits at or below the BASE case; oil-equivalent production +0.2% in Q4 2022, forward revenues +12.3% (no Q1 2023 revenue guide, Q4 2022 revenue as reported); the energy transition is live and re-filed: the theme registry dates its market pricing to ExxonMobil's removal from the Dow Jones Industrial Average (effective 2020-08-31).
